subject: Procurement lane recommendation — public marketplace vs direct private offer
messages:

Subject: Procurement lane guidance — Redwood subscription

Diego,

Thanks for running the pilot with our team. Procurement here at Greenbridge asked me to confirm the recommended purchase path for production: should we buy via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace (public listing or private offer) or do a direct contract / invoice?

Key constraints from procurement:
- We need monthly invoicing and PO-based billing (our AP team cannot do annual prepay without special approvals).
- We want to understand co-sell incentives (how/when partner credits flow back to Redwood or our account team) — this affects total cost of ownership.
- Timeline: we aim to have the legal/finance path decided before Jan 10 so we can onboard in January.

Can you outline tradeoffs (billing cadence, contract length, co-sell eligibility, procurement friction) and any paperwork we should expect if we choose marketplace vs direct? Also any preferences for AWS vs Azure vs GCP for co-sell?

Appreciate a short summary and whether a single 30-min call with procurement + sales ops would help.

Best,

Greenbridge Health

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Filing a concise comparison below and attaching a short one-pager that we use with procurement. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your procurement/finance team to walk through details.

Summary (marketplace vs direct invoice/private offer)

1) Public Marketplace (standard listing)
- Billing cadence: Typically monthly via the marketplace (billed through the marketplace provider). PO acceptance varies by marketplace and customer — marketplaces often require the purchaser to accept marketplace terms; some AP teams can reconcile marketplace invoices against POs but there can be delays.
- Co-sell: Public listings generally make you eligible for partner programs but co-sell credits/incentives are limited compared to private offers/co-sell programs.
- Time to onboard: Fastest for procurement teams that accept marketplace invoices.
- Tradeoffs: Lower friction for sales/ops, but less flexibility on custom contractual terms and support SLAs.

2) Marketplace Private Offer (PMO / Private Offer / AWS Private Marketplace)
- Billing cadence: Can be configured to match monthly or annual billing; however the marketplace provider still mediates invoicing.
- Co-sell: Best option if you want to capture marketplace co-sell incentives while retaining some custom pricing/terms. Requires setting up a private offer and approval flow with our marketplace partner (AWS/Azure/GCP).
- Time to onboard: Slightly slower than public listing (setup + acceptance of private offer).
- Tradeoffs: Good middle ground — preserves co-sell eligibility and allows negotiated pricing; may add a step for procurement to accept the private offer.

3) Direct contract / Redwood invoice (direct purchase)
- Billing cadence: Fully flexible — we can accept monthly POs and invoice per agreed schedule.
- Co-sell: Typically not eligible for cloud marketplace co-sell incentives; if co-sell credit is important we can pursue alternative partner credit agreements but execution differs by provider.
- Time to onboard: Slower if legal needs custom MSA; faster if you accept our standard redwood SOW + PO process.
- Tradeoffs: Maximum contractual flexibility (SLAs, data residency, custom terms) but requires direct contracting and potentially longer legal review.

Provider notes:
- AWS: Most mature co-sell programs and predictable Private Offer workflows — recommended if you want the co-sell program benefit.
- Azure: Good for enterprise customers already aligned to Azure Marketplace; co-sell cadence can be strong but process differs by region/company.
- GCP: Improving marketplace features; co-sell programs are less standardized than AWS today.

Recommendation (based on Greenbridge constraints):
- If your AP team can accept marketplace invoices monthly, a Marketplace Private Offer (AWS PMO preferred if you use AWS) gives the best balance: retains co-sell benefits and permits negotiated terms.
- If you need explicit PO-based monthly invoices with no intermediary, go direct and we’ll provide monthly invoices keyed to your PO number — but you may lose marketplace co-sell credits.

Next steps
- I attached a one-pager (Redwood-procurement-options-20261220.pdf) that procurement teams find helpful.
- Proposed: 30-min call next week with your procurement + our sales ops to confirm preferred billing cadence and to outline the private offer acceptance steps.

Thanks — I’ll let Vanessa loop in the co-sell specifics.

Thanks Diego — helpful overview. A couple quick clarifications from procurement and finance:

- Co-sell credit flow: If we buy via Private Offer on AWS, how and when do co-sell credits show up for the account team? Do credits reduce our invoice or are they remitted separately to Redwood as a partner incentive?
- PO acceptance: We generally push a monthly PO to vendors and expect an invoice referencing that PO. If the marketplace mediates invoicing, will the marketplace invoice include our PO number so AP can match?
- Cancellation/termination windows: For private offers that are annual with monthly invoicing, what is the typical early termination clause?

If you can confirm those three items, we can choose between private offer vs direct. We’re leaning to private offer if co-sell gives discounts/credits that flow to Redwood (helps your team) and if our AP can still do PO+monthly.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — if helpful we can do the 30-min call after you confirm the above.

Hi Sana / Alex — quick answers to your points (pulling from our Marketplace & Co-sell playbook):

1) Co-sell credit flow (AWS Private Offer)
- Credits/incentives for AWS co-sell typically accrue to the partner (Redwood) and are reconciled between AWS and Redwood. They do not reduce the customer-facing invoice directly. In practice, co-sell benefits offset Redwood's chargebacks or influence our go-to-market rebates, not your invoice line item.

2) PO on marketplace invoices
- In many cases the marketplace invoice supports PO numbers in the invoice metadata if the buyer includes the PO during purchase/acceptance; however this varies by marketplace and buyer workflow. For AWS Private Offer we can request that your PO number be captured at acceptance so the marketplace invoice includes the PO reference for AP matching. We will confirm the exact field mapping during the onboarding call.

3) Termination windows
- Private Offer terms are negotiable: common approaches are annual term with 30/60-day termination for convenience or 90-day early-termination fee based on remaining committed value. For direct contracts we can flex to your standard termination language with a negotiated SOW.

Recommendation: Given Greenbridge’s need for monthly PO-based invoices and desire to preserve co-sell incentives, start with an AWS Private Offer configured for monthly billing and include the PO-metadata capture step. That gives you the co-sell GTM advantages while letting AP reconcile invoices to POs.

Next steps (let’s coordinate):

- Diego — can you propose 3 time slots for a 30-min onboarding call next week?
